dedupe_keys.name: powersume interface bringing assume reinforcement learning to other electricity market models

description: PowerSUME is interface code that lets other agent-based electricity market models use the reinforcement learning bidding agents of the ASSUME framework. It was released in March 2026 (version 0.1.0) by Thorsten Weiskopf, Kim K. Miskiw, Niklas Treml and Jonathan Stelzer, with copyright held by the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. An external market model sends power plant data and forecasts to PowerSUME over an HTTP interface; PowerSUME manages the learning environment and, using ASSUME, returns bids, following documented endpoints and a data contract. The authors recommend it only when an existing market model brings features beyond ASSUME's own market simulation, and otherwise advise using ASSUME directly. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and downloadable from Zenodo under the GNU AGPL 3.0 at no cost. Caveats: it relies on a specific ASSUME commit, passes only a single price per unit and always offers the maximum available capacity, and needs a separate market model that implements the interface. Simulation uses are agent-based studies of strategic bidding in electricity markets. Related records: model-assume is the framework it connects to.
